newsitem.title: FRANCE: Usinor sees 1996 loss at Unimetal unit.
newsitem.headline: Usinor sees 1996 loss at Unimetal unit.

text.p: Usinor Sacilor said on Wednesday its long metals unit Unimetal may lose money again this year.
Bernard Rogy, chairman of the special steels holding Aster, made the forecast to journalists on Tuesday, an Usinor spokeswoman said.
Unimetal, which lost 540 million francs last year, may incur losses of roughly the same order in 1996, he said.
Unimetal's performance was hurt by a slowdown in demand and by technical problems linked to the startup of a new electric furnace.
The unit embarked in 1995 on a tough cost-cutting plan aimed at saving some 750 million francs by end 1997.
Rogy said savings generated by the plan may reach 850 million francs by mid-1998.
In September, Usinor's Chairman Francis Mer put losses incurred by Unimetal in the first half of 1996 at "several hundred million francs" but predicted a better performance in 1997.
